correctness.rationale: The product of T_s triangles plus an optional terminal interval contains P_d^(s). The product circumball has unique center and radius from block geometry; two feasible mutually antipodal points force optimality, uniqueness and diameter 2R. Strict convexity shows contacts must be container vertices. Even-index bounds are equivalent to no adjacent positives for integer s>=2, so contacts correspond bijectively to path independent sets (F_(d+2)); when s=1 all product corners survive except odd-dimensional terminal restrictions (3^r or 5*3^(r-1)). Antipodal corners in each triangle must be (s,0)/(0,s); cross-interface feasibility forces one unordered orientation pair for s>=2, whereas s=1 leaves 2^(r-1). Independently enumerated all block-corner contacts and antipodal pairs for 36 (d,s) instances, including d=2,3; finite checks corroborate but do not establish arbitrary d.

value.rationale: Complete equality-case geometry reveals a sharp discrete transition at s=2 and an exponential-to-unique collapse in diametral pairs within a natural recently studied lattice-polytope family. The radius is elementary from a product relaxation; the boundary-contact classification and all unordered diametral configurations are the substantive original invariants, potentially useful when studying extremal Euclidean geometry of these polytopes.

limitations: Integer twist s>=1 and noncyclic constraints only; not a claim for arbitrary real twist.
Original full motivating preprint and a possible general contact classification remain priority risks.
